symtable.SymbolTable.get_id() returns id() of the underlying object: stable WITHIN a process, different ACROSS processes. Emitting it verbatim would make every golden file differ run-to-run, violating Appendix B invariant #5. Caught by the harness self-test before any golden file existed. The oracle now emits a canonical pre-order ordinal instead, which fully serves the column's documented purpose (schema v6 section 2.2 c11: 'oracle cross-check handle only; never joined on'). IMPORTANT FOR A3. Scope-introducing nodes inside a function's defaults, decorators, parameter annotations, return annotation, or a class's bases/keywords are evaluated in the ENCLOSING scope, so symtable makes them SIBLINGS of the def/class, not children. Same for the OUTERMOST iterable of a comprehension. 'def f(x=lambda: 1)' -> the lambda is a child of f's parent. A walker that stops descending at a scope node loses them: found by sweeping the oracle over sqlalchemy, 34 of 563 files failed. Fixed in emit_oracle.py via _enclosing_evaluated_parts / _owned_scope_nodes; the parser must replicate this or its scope tree will be wrong on ~6% of real files.

THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS FALSE and I have implemented the corrected assertion. Asked to assert that 'symtable child order matches ast source order'. It does not: symtable orders children by symbol-table CONSTRUCTION order. For 'def outer(): @d(lambda:DEC) / def f(x=lambda:DEF, *, y: C[lambda:ANN]=2)' symtable yields [lambda@3, lambda@3, lambda@2, f@3] - not source order and not even line order. Asserting source order would fail on real code for the wrong reason. VERIFIED ON 3.10.4, these gaps FORCED values into tier 1 that would otherwise be tier 2. (1) typing.get_overloads does NOT exist before 3.11, so @overload stubs are INVISIBLE at runtime - only the final implementation is in __dict__. OVERLOAD_STUB is therefore ast-only. (2) typing.final does NOT set __final__ before 3.11, so the FINAL modifier has no runtime witness and is ast-only. (3) inspect.getmembers_static does not exist on 3.10, so introspection must read cls.__dict__ directly - which is also safer, since attribute access invokes descriptors. (4) A class-body lambda is an ordinary function at runtime, indistinguishable from a def; only ast sees it.
